## Root cause summary

Two interacting production defects:

1. **Time/expiry semantics — `HeartbeatPolicy.expired`**: computed `nowMillis/1000 - lastHeartbeatMillis`, i.e. it divided the millisecond clock down to seconds before subtracting a millisecond timestamp. The difference was essentially always a large negative number, so sessions with a 5s timeout never expired (and the comparison mixed units). Fixed to `nowMillis - lastHeartbeatMillis > timeoutMillis` — all-millisecond arithmetic.

Fixed to construct the fresh session and `registry.put(fresh)` instead of removing it, so a reconnected session always remains registered.

Together they caused the regression: because expiry never fired, stale sessions were silently "reconnected" in place; and when expiry did fire (e.g. after a manual timeout change), the session was dropped from the registry entirely.

## Root cause summary

Two interacting production defects:

1. **Time/expiry semantics — `HeartbeatPolicy.expired`**: computed `nowMillis/1000 - lastHeartbeatMillis`, i.e. it divided the millisecond clock down to seconds before subtracting a millisecond timestamp. The difference was essentially always a large negative number, so sessions with a 5s timeout never expired (and the comparison mixed units). Fixed to `nowMillis - lastHeartbeatMillis > timeoutMillis` — all-millisecond arithmetic.

2. **State transition/reconnect — `ReconnectCoordinator.reconnect` (expired branch)**: on expiry it called `registry.remove(id)` and returned a brand-new `Session` *without re-registering it*. The log shows the consequence: `reconnect returned connected object but registry lookup is null` — the caller held a "connected" object while the registry no longer knew the session (leak/inconsistency). Fixed to construct the fresh session and `registry.put(fresh)` instead of removing it, so a reconnected session always remains registered.

Together they caused the regression: because expiry never fired, stale sessions were silently "reconnected" in place; and when expiry did fire (e.g. after a manual timeout change), the session was dropped from the registry entirely.
